portInfo.description: Western Crete’s Chania has a layered Venetian and Ottoman old town, a historic seafront and a newer museum district at Halepa. Souda is the port-side starting point for this guide; the old harbour in the photographs is a different place. A relaxed day can combine the harbour lanes with one museum or Nea Hora, without turning the call into an all-island coach marathon.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Old Venetian Harbour and lighthouse view, Landward promenade facing the Egyptian lighthouse, Old Harbour, Chania: A specific seafront focus for the city’s Venetian and later maritime layers. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Do not assume the outer breakwater/lighthouse interior is accessible.

Splantzia old-town streets, Splantzia district square/lanes, old Chania: An Ottoman-era neighbourhood contrast to the open waterfront. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Use an agreed square-side meeting point; lanes may have uneven paving.

Archaeological Museum of Chania, Archaeological Museum, Halepa, Chania: Use the current Halepa museum location rather than the former old-town address. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). Confirm admission/opening day and accessible transfer.

Eleftherios Venizelos house museum, Venizelos house museum, Halepa, Chania: A focused modern-history visit within the Halepa quarter. Allow about 75 minutes (editorial estimate). Separate museum admission; not guaranteed by entry to the archaeological museum.

Nea Hora seafront and beach, Nea Hora beach/harbour promenade, Chania: A nearby coastal pause with a different pace from the historic lanes. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Swimming, facilities and public access depend on conditions; retain Souda pickup time.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Tell the driver “Souda cruise passenger gate” and show the ship’s pickup instructions, not merely “Chania harbour.” An old-town taxi rank and the cruise berth are not the same destination.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Port of Souda — passenger-port complex — Souda port,Souda,Chania
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The Greek ports association places Souda 7 km from the city centre and lists passenger stations, bus/taxi access and ISPS arrangements. Its regional Port Fund portfolio covers many harbours; those are not all Chania cruise terminals. Allow 45 minutes outward for assigned Souda exit plus bus/taxi to the old-town edge, and up to 60 minutes on return including pickup, traffic and port entry. These are planning allowances, not a verified current bus schedule. Halepa requires another local transfer or a longer walk; do not send passengers to an obsolete museum address in the old town.
